sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is sufficient; no master’s required. Apply to PhD: the new SM route is for MIT
mathematics undergraduates, so do not use its 4.8 GPA/course checklist for a UChicago application. [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create application; enter field interests and education/work history, math/science/engineering grades,
objectives and potential outside funding. Notify referees early; departmental planning advice is before 15
November. Shortlisted applicants have January Zoom interviews. [s1] [s2]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Prospective informal faculty visits allowed; no prior advisor commitment required by published steps.
Distinguish informal visit from the January shortlisted Zoom interview. [s2]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Department FAQ permits adding new information/comments after submission. Recommender procedures
depend on GradApply; central Slate instructions are not automatically transferable. [s2] [s6]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Current pages include 2026 fee-waiver date and January interviews; main deadline sentence is annual, and
stipends remain labeled 2025-26. [s1] [s2] [s3]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Department publishes 1 December, 23:59 EST; FAQ says all letters/supporting documents due 1 December.
The same page contains a 20 November 2026 fee-waiver deadline, but the main application deadline sentence
omits its year; treat 1 December 2026 as current-cycle inference pending portal confirmation. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Same application; no separate departmental funding application. External fellowship deadlines independent.
[s1]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Department says take required IELTS/TOEFL by 31 December, later than its 1 December supporting-document
date. This inconsistency needs confirmation if no waiver. GRE optional. [s1] [s2]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Central policy holds MIT funded offers open until at least 15 April; exact 2027 offer deadline and possible
extension must be read in offer. [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
IELTS preferred; minimum IELTS 7.0 in math FAQ. Department also accepts TOEFL iBT and DET; generally not
TOEFL PBT. TOEFL reporting institution 3514, department 72. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Central exemption applies to a recent English-taught undergraduate degree from the United States (within five
years). For a degree still in progress, inspect portal eligibility; any waiver request is embedded in application.
Departments can request supplementary English evidence even when exempt. [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Entirely optional; scores accepted, and department explicitly says omission will not hurt the application. Math
Subject result is the GRE component of greatest interest. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three or more recommenders, with official electronic letters. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate departmental funding application; no extra scholarship essay/reference stated for ordinary
admission support. External fellowships may require their own materials. [s1]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
Important platform distinction: central OGE says mathematics uses GradApply and applicant must notify
referees using provided emails/links. Math page says writer instructions generated after submitting. General
Slate auto-send guidance must not be assumed for math; check actual GradApply controls before submission.
[s1] [s5] [s6]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
Math departmental wording indicates instructions after submission; OGE math-specific FAQ assigns notification
responsibility to applicant. Exact current trigger unresolved publicly. [s1] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Not established from the public sources reviewed. Verify in the current application or with graduate admissions
before relying on this item.
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Central policy: letters cannot be shared across MIT applications; cannot add recommenders or change contact
details after submission; FERPA choice locks when request sent. Confirm how these central rules map to math
GradApply. [s5]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published 2025-26 only: fellowship USD 4,370.21/month; TA/RA USD 4,488.28/month; Instructor G USD
5,024.73/month. September-May support plus one summer fellowship month at 85% of current rate; additional
summer support via mentoring/RA/fellowship is separate. Full tuition and 12-month individual health coverage.
Do not multiply monthly rate by 12 as a guaranteed annual award. 2027-28 rates not verified. [s3]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five-year guarantee while making satisfactory progress. First year full fellowship, no teaching duties. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Explicitly includes international admitted students. [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory progress; students expected to teach at least one semester. TA work generally 10-12 hours/week.
Additional summer support is not identical to guaranteed academic-year support. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate departmental funding application; no extra scholarship essay/reference stated for ordinary
admission support. External fellowships may require their own materials. [s1]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Outside fellowships encouraged; department supplements partial outside support to standard support level.
Conference travel allowance from year two. [s3]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 90 by credit/debit card. [s1]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Request in application by 20 November 2026. Public math pages do not fully enumerate international eligibility
or documentation; inspect embedded request before paying. [s1] [s2]

Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written

Pay attention to
• Do not confuse MIT internal SM admission with PhD admission.
• Math GradApply has special reference instructions.
• Published stipend is 2025-26, with only one guaranteed summer month at 85% rate.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is sufficient; no master’s required. Apply to PhD: the new SM route is for MIT
mathematics undergraduates, so do not use its 4.8 GPA/course checklist for a UChicago application. [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create application; enter field interests and education/work history, math/science/engineering grades,
objectives and potential outside funding. Notify referees early; departmental planning advice is before 15
November. Shortlisted applicants have January Zoom interviews. [s1] [s2]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Prospective informal faculty visits allowed; no prior advisor commitment required by published steps.
Distinguish informal visit from the January shortlisted Zoom interview. [s2]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Department FAQ permits adding new information/comments after submission. Recommender procedures
depend on GradApply; central Slate instructions are not automatically transferable. [s2] [s6]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Current pages include 2026 fee-waiver date and January interviews; main deadline sentence is annual, and
stipends remain labeled 2025-26. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Department publishes 1 December, 23:59 EST; FAQ says all letters/supporting documents due 1 December.
The same page contains a 20 November 2026 fee-waiver deadline, but the main application deadline sentence
omits its year; treat 1 December 2026 as current-cycle inference pending portal confirmation. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Same application; no separate departmental funding application. External fellowship deadlines independent.
[s1]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Department says take required IELTS/TOEFL by 31 December, later than its 1 December supporting-document
date. This inconsistency needs confirmation if no waiver. GRE optional. [s1] [s2]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Central policy holds MIT funded offers open until at least 15 April; exact 2027 offer deadline and possible
extension must be read in offer. [s7]

English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
IELTS preferred; minimum IELTS 7.0 in math FAQ. Department also accepts TOEFL iBT and DET; generally not
TOEFL PBT. TOEFL reporting institution 3514, department 72. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Central exemption applies to a recent English-taught undergraduate degree from the United States (within five
years). For a degree still in progress, inspect portal eligibility; any waiver request is embedded in application.
Departments can request supplementary English evidence even when exempt. [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Entirely optional; scores accepted, and department explicitly says omission will not hurt the application. Math
Subject result is the GRE component of greatest interest. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload undergraduate transcript electronic copy; official transcript requested only after admission. Enter
grades in mathematics/science/engineering and overall grades. [s1] [s2]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Application collects mathematics/science/engineering coursework grades. Public page does not give the
course-entry template or separate file formatting/length. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Not specified as separate required uploads on the PhD public checklist. Exact current portal prompts/limits and
optional paper upload/link permissions require confirmation; do not use the internal SM checklist. [s1] [s2]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three or more recommenders, with official electronic letters. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate departmental funding application; no extra scholarship essay/reference stated for ordinary
admission support. External fellowships may require their own materials. [s1]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
Important platform distinction: central OGE says mathematics uses GradApply and applicant must notify
referees using provided emails/links. Math page says writer instructions generated after submitting. General
Slate auto-send guidance must not be assumed for math; check actual GradApply controls before submission.
[s1] [s5] [s6]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
Math departmental wording indicates instructions after submission; OGE math-specific FAQ assigns notification
responsibility to applicant. Exact current trigger unresolved publicly. [s1] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Not established from the public sources reviewed. Verify in the current application or with graduate admissions
before relying on this item.
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Central policy: letters cannot be shared across MIT applications; cannot add recommenders or change contact
details after submission; FERPA choice locks when request sent. Confirm how these central rules map to math
GradApply. [s5]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Personal / background statement; Research proposal; Writing sample /
thesis / research summary; Publications list; Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Not specified as separate required uploads on the PhD public checklist. Exact current portal prompts/limits and

Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Statement of objectives/research statement required. Public departmental page does not expose exact full
prompt, word/page limit or formatting; retrieve in current application before drafting. [s1] [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Field(s) of interest and statement of objectives requested; research potential is emphasized. No separate
proposal template established. [s1] [s2]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Application collects mathematics/science/engineering coursework grades. Public page does not give the
course-entry template or separate file formatting/length. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate departmental funding application; no extra scholarship essay/reference stated for ordinary
admission support. External fellowships may require their own materials. [s1]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published 2025-26 only: fellowship USD 4,370.21/month; TA/RA USD 4,488.28/month; Instructor G USD
5,024.73/month. September-May support plus one summer fellowship month at 85% of current rate; additional
summer support via mentoring/RA/fellowship is separate. Full tuition and 12-month individual health coverage.
Do not multiply monthly rate by 12 as a guaranteed annual award. 2027-28 rates not verified. [s3]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five-year guarantee while making satisfactory progress. First year full fellowship, no teaching duties. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Explicitly includes international admitted students. [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Satisfactory progress; students expected to teach at least one semester. TA work generally 10-12 hours/week.
Additional summer support is not identical to guaranteed academic-year support. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate departmental funding application; no extra scholarship essay/reference stated for ordinary
admission support. External fellowships may require their own materials. [s1]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Outside fellowships encouraged; department supplements partial outside support to standard support level.
Conference travel allowance from year two. [s3]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 90 by credit/debit card. [s1]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Request in application by 20 November 2026. Public math pages do not fully enumerate international eligibility
or documentation; inspect embedded request before paying. [s1] [s2]
